EXPORT_NAME is the safe rename axis: it propagates identically to both the Config file's imported target and the CPS component key, unlike NAMESPACE — a 4.3.4/4.4.2 consumer linking the EXPORT_NAME spelling builds cleanly.

surprises: A shared OUTPUT_NAME across Debug/Release means `cmake --install --config Release` silently overwrites the file `--config Debug` already installed — both per-config export files then import the identical (Release) binary, with no error at either install step.

A consumer requesting a CMake config absent from the install does NOT fail loudly by default — it silently falls back to whatever config exists and links/runs it; only an explicit empty CMAKE_MAP_IMPORTED_CONFIG_<CONFIG> turns this into a hard Generate-step error.

CPS's install(PACKAGE_INFO) completely ignores the install(EXPORT) NAMESPACE — it always names the component after its own argument, so a namespace mismatching by case only silently breaks every ≥4.3 consumer of the old namespace, while ≤4.3 consumers keep working.

CPS's cross-package `requires.<dep>.hints` field bakes the literal, un-relativized install prefix into the exported .cps file (a real relocation leak) — but the existing CMK-INST-01 leak grep already catches it unmodified, and the leak turns out to be functionally harmless because CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH search wins over the stale hint.

top_rules: Set BUILD_SHARED_LIBS as a CACHE entry (-D or set(...CACHE...FORCE)) before FetchContent/add_subdirectory, never as a plain set() normal variable — a normal-variable setting is silently discarded (only a policy warning, no error) by any dependency whose own cmake_minimum_required predates 3.13 (CMP0077), measured on 3.31.12 and 4.4.2

Never claim CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE 'guarantees' PIC: it only seeds the property when a target is created and has no effect on a target that already sets POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE itself or was created before the set() call

A static library that may be linked into a SHARED/MODULE target must have PIC resolved to ON before the target is created (via -D, normal-var set() before add_subdirectory, or set() before FetchContent_MakeAvailable) — baseline with no PIC anywhere fails with 'relocation R_X86_64_32S ... recompile with -fPIC', exit 1, identically on 3.31.12 and 4.4.2
A library never forces BUILD_SHARED_LIBS on itself — read it via option(BUILD_SHARED_LIBS ... <default>) with no CACHE...FORCE, generalizing CMK-BZL-07 beyond the Bazel-wrap scope

An installable shared library sets CXX_VISIBILITY_PRESET hidden + VISIBILITY_INLINES_HIDDEN ON with GenerateExportHeader; without it every symbol including a header-only inline function is exported by default from an ELF .so (measured via nm -D --defined-only, before/after)
WINDOWS_EXPORT_ALL_SYMBOLS is Windows/MS-toolchain-only and never a Linux/macOS substitute for visibility hardening, and even on Windows does not cover data symbols or every virtual-function case

Before turning CMAKE_LINK_LIBRARIES_ONLY_TARGETS ON, convert every bare system-library link item (m, pthread, dl, rt) to an imported target or absolute path — the flag cannot distinguish a legitimate bare name from a typo and rejects both with an identical 'which is not a target' generate-time error, exit 1 (measured on 4.4.2)

There is no CMAKE_DEBUG_PREFIX_MAP; reproducible-build path stripping is manual via -ffile-prefix-map through target_compile_options or a toolchain file's CMAKE_<LANG>_FLAGS_INIT — both measured to produce byte-identical objects from two different absolute source/build directories
surprises: The real silent failure in this whole dive is BUILD_SHARED_LIBS, not PIC: a parent's set(BUILD_SHARED_LIBS ON) normal variable before FetchContent is silently overridden back to a fetched dependency's own option()-declared default when that dependency's floor predates CMake 3.13 (CMP0077), with only a policy warning and no error — confirmed on both 3.31.12 and 4.4.2

A trivial static function returning a constant does NOT trigger the classic 'recompile with -fPIC' link failure on this host's GCC 15.2.1 (RIP-relative addressing already covers it) — a genuine reproducer needed a global array-of-pointers indexed dynamically, which produces R_X86_64_32S in .text under default (no -fPIC) codegen on this Fedora/RHEL-style toolchain

The wave-2 install-round-trip-and-cps.md §10 measurement that claimed 'PIC reached the archive' never actually linked the static archive into a shared library (BASE_SHARED=OFF) — it could not have observed link success or failure either way, so it is not evidence for the M-E-09 claim at all, just for '-fPIC appears on the compile line when passed as -D'

CMAKE_LINK_LIBRARIES_ONLY_TARGETS treats the bare system-library names 'm' and 'pthread' identically to a misspelled target name — enabling this 3.23 hardening flag on an existing project is a breaking change, not a pure typo-catcher, unless bare system libraries are pre-converted to imported targets

The CMAKE_LINK_LIBRARIES_ONLY_TARGETS diagnostic fires at CMake's generate phase (after 'Configuring done' prints) rather than at the target_link_libraries call site during configure, so a log-substring check anchored before 'Configuring done' would miss it

-ffile-prefix-map via target_compile_options() and via a toolchain file's CMAKE_C_FLAGS_INIT are fully equivalent and both produce byte-identical .o files across two different absolute source/build directories — there is no CMake-native CMAKE_DEBUG_PREFIX_MAP abstraction at all

top_rules: Diagnose "which copy resolved" from CMakeCache.txt's <Pkg>_DIR vs current <Pkg>_ROOT, never from --debug-find-pkg alone -- a cached valid _DIR short-circuits the debug output into looking clean
On CMake >=4.1 read CMakeConfigureLog.yaml's find_package-v1 found.path before trusting a resolution; the event doesn't exist below 4.1
Never use cmake --graphviz to diagnose which package/prefix resolved -- measured to show only the target-link graph
cmake -L omits UNINITIALIZED cache entries (an unpromoted -D<Pkg>_ROOT); grep CMakeCache.txt directly instead

Prove package consumability by linking a real compiled target, never by a green install or a LANGUAGES NONE smoke consumer -- a missing find_dependency() is invisible until Generate needs a real link line
Never design a dependency-provider integration on find_program/find_library seeing the provider's paths -- cmake-conan leaves CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH empty before and after the intercepted find_package
cmake_language(DEFER CALL find_package ...) fires at the END of the current listfile, never earlier -- it cannot rescue an earlier find_program
A dependency floor below 3.5 needs CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM set to 3.10 (not 3.5) scoped around the one call, to clear both the hard-error and the deprecation tier

On 3.x, the only remedies that keep -Werror=dev fully live for a stale-floor dependency are a FetchContent PATCH_COMMAND rewriting the floor or a re-pin to >=3.10 -- -Wno-error=deprecated does not clear a dev-escalated deprecation and CMAKE_WARN_DEPRECATED OFF survives but silences the project's own deprecations too
vcpkg's toolchain has no staleness protection of its own: repointing VCPKG_INSTALLED_DIR leaves <pkg>_DIR stuck on the old prefix, identical to the plain-CMake CMK-DEP-13 case
surprises: Measured correction to the wave-2 consolidation: CMAKE_WARN_DEPRECATED=OFF DOES survive -Werror=dev on 3.31.12 (reproduced twice) -- contradicts CMK-DEP-15's stated mechanism, though the practical ban stands for a sharper reason: it also silences the project's own deprecation warnings under the identical flag
-Wno-error=deprecated does not clear a cmake_minimum_required-floor deprecation when -Werror=dev is also set, in either flag order -- the warning is independently escalated by the dev category

cmake_language(DEFER) does not help the find_program-before-find_package sequencing problem at all; it defers to the END of the listfile, so DEFER-wrapping the find_package makes it fire even later than an unwrapped call would

The real cmake-conan provider never touches CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH in either direction -- it satisfies the intercepted find_package by injecting the target directly, so no find_program/find_library ever sees Conan's paths regardless of ordering

conan graph explain errors with 'There is no missing binary' against a normal resolved graph -- it is not a general graph reader, only a missing/mismatched-binary explainer; conan graph info is the general tool

A missing find_dependency() in an installed Config produces a fully green configure for both the exporter and a LANGUAGES NONE/interface-only consumer; the failure only appears at a downstream Generate step when a real compiled target actually links

conflicts_resolved: Dive candidate 3 (explicit-empty CMAKE_MAP_IMPORTED_CONFIG_<CONFIG> as the loud-failure switch) is refuted. The empty element means the configuration-less IMPORTED_LOCATION, so it also rejects a correctly installed configuration (configure exit 1 on 3.31.12 and 4.4.2, run-map-variants.sh). CMK-INST-22 pins the map to the configuration itself instead.

Dive section 7 and exemplar claim that rapidjson's export(PACKAGE) is a no-op: refuted. rapidjson's floor is 3.5, CMP0090 is unset, and its real CMakeLists writes ~/.cmake/packages/RapidJSON on 3.31.12 and 4.4.2 (run-export-package-floor.sh). This produced new CMK-INST-24 (MUST) and a correction to failure mode 12 ('off by default since 3.15' is true only for floors of 3.15 or later).
Dive section 3 said the silent configuration fallback is 'undocumented'. Corrected: the IMPORTED_LOCATION help at 4.4.2 allows selecting any other IMPORTED_CONFIGURATIONS entry.
Dive section 3 said a multi-config Generate error surfaces in a later, separate step. Refuted: cmake -S -B itself exits 1.

Dive section 2 CPS hints leak versus CMK-INST-01 step (a), which looked like a clash with CMK-INST-14. Resolved without weakening step (a): the hint is the dependency's absolute <dep>_DIR. Step (a) flags it only when the dependency lies inside the tree under test, which is a true finding (run-cps-hints.sh: separate prefix gives no hit, same prefix gives a hit, on 4.3.4 and 4.4.2). A hand-run over a multi-package prefix is documented as expected.

Dive candidate 9 (POST_BUILD $<TARGET_RUNTIME_DLLS> copy as the Windows install fix) was a build-tree mechanism. It is replaced by CMK-INST-23, grounded in install.rst: a DLL is a RUNTIME artefact, and naming only ARCHIVE or LIBRARY installs no DLL. RUNTIME_DEPENDENCY_SET is kept as an application-only note, measured on Linux.

Dive candidate 1 (per-config OUTPUT_NAME, checked by md5) is replaced by CMAKE_DEBUG_POSTFIX/DEBUG_POSTFIX plus a static duplicate-IMPORTED_LOCATION scan, measured to fire without a postfix and stay empty with one.
CMK-INST-15 'comparison' framing: CPS never reads NAMESPACE, so the match is exact, case included. EXPORT_NAME is honoured by both generators. The rule text was changed in place.

Dive candidate 7 (CMAKE_POLICY_DEFAULT_CMP0090 is a no-op) is scoped to floors of 3.15 or later, where nothing needs suppressing. It became failure mode 15, pointing to CMAKE_EXPORT_NO_PACKAGE_REGISTRY as vcpkg uses it, not a rule.
Dive candidate 10 (CMP0207 slash-class regex) is not adopted: a smell, not a defect. The CMP0207 warning did not fire on Linux under the configure gate on 3.31.12, 4.3.4 or 4.4.2.

top_rules: A cross toolchain MUST explicitly set FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_LIBRARY/INCLUDE/PACKAGE to ONLY -- the unset default is BOTH (measured), not ONLY, and silently falls through to host copies
Never override FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_PROGRAM away from its NEVER default -- ONLY/BOTH breaks CMake's own CMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM search, not just find_program
CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR only auto-wires onto real add_executable targets in add_test(NAME...COMMAND); set_tests_properties(...CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR...) on a script-path test is silently inert

A module's <Name>_ROOT CACHE FORCE hint (CMK-MOD-12/find_ocx pattern) does NOT survive a manager's CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH injection (vcpkg) or forced BOTH mode (Conan) -- CMK-MOD-12's guarantee must be qualified
Conan 2.32.0's CMakeToolchain FindFiles block force-rewrites ONLY to BOTH under cross_building, which can let a pre-existing sysroot copy shadow Conan's own resolved package

project(LANGUAGES NONE) leaves CMAKE_SIZEOF_VOID_P unset, silently disabling lib64 candidates in find_package(CONFIG) regardless of CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH or <Pkg>_ROOT -- the fix is enabling a language, not repointing the hint
FindPkgConfig.cmake never references PKG_CONFIG_SYSROOT_DIR or PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR -- a cross build must set both by hand or a found .pc file will emit host-rooted include/lib paths
A project()-level command inside a VCPKG_CHAINLOAD_TOOLCHAIN_FILE/Conan user_toolchain file is a hard 'Recursive call not allowed' configure error, not a silent misbehavior

Toolchain files are read 2 (project()) + 1 (compiler ABI try_compile) + N (whole-project try_compile calls) times per configure -- budget side effects accordingly; the SOURCES-only try_compile signature never re-reads it
vcpkg's VCPKG_TOOLCHAIN self-guard protects only its own setup code -- a chainloaded file via VCPKG_CHAINLOAD_TOOLCHAIN_FILE re-runs on every one of those reads, not just the first
surprises: The true default for CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_LIBRARY/INCLUDE/PACKAGE when a toolchain sets none is BOTH, not ONLY -- overturning the topic map's own M-H-05 framing and the widely-copied cmake-toolchains(7) worked-example assumption; isolated with a package that exists only in a host prefix (find_package(onlyhost) still resolves it)

CMake's rooted-vs-unrooted search under BOTH/ONLY runs a full rooted pass across ALL 9 find_package search-order categories before any unrooted candidate is tried -- so a manager-injected CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH entry (or even the sysroot's own default /usr) can shadow a nominally-higher-priority <Name>_ROOT hint or CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH entry

Conan 2 deliberately overrides ONLY to BOTH for cross builds (never touches CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH itself) -- confirmed in real generated conan_toolchain.cmake from a live conan install -- and this reopens a 'silently resolve the sysroot's own copy instead of Conan's' trap

CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR is a TARGET property baked into add_test() at generate time; setting it via set_tests_properties on a script-path test is accepted syntax that CTest never reads at runtime -- verified live with a real emulator wrapper that only fired for the target-based test

try_compile()'s nested configure output is captured, not forwarded -- a message(STATUS) marker in a toolchain file undercounts re-reads during try_compile; only a file(APPEND) sink revealed the true count (5 reads for 2 whole-project try_compiles, vs. 2 visible in console output)

FindPkgConfig.cmake's own lib64/multiarch pkgconfig-dir guessing is skipped entirely when actually cross-compiling, falling back to pure PKG_CONFIG_PATH/LIBDIR passthrough with zero CMAKE_SYSROOT awareness
